root_cause.text: The TLS TX work cancellation path in `tls_sw_cancel_work_tx()` used `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` on `ctx->tx_work.work`, which waits for the current run to finish but does not prevent concurrent re-scheduling of the delayed work, allowing `tx_work_handler()` to run after `tls_sk_proto_close()` has begun freeing the TLS context.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message show that after `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` is called from `tls_sk_proto_close()`, `tls_write_space()`/`tls_sw_write_space()` can still call `schedule_delayed_work(&tx_ctx->tx_work.work, 0)` on another CPU, leading to a race where `tx_work_handler()` dereferences a freed TLS object; the patch fixes this by replacing `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` with `disable_delayed_work_sync()` in `net/tls/tls_sw.c`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace TX work cancellation with disable_delayed_work_sync() to fully stop and prevent rescheduling of TLS TX delayed work.
intent_record.what: In tls_sw_cancel_work_tx(), the call to cancel_delayed_work_sync(&ctx->tx_work.work) was replaced with disable_delayed_work_sync(&ctx->tx_work.work).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the TX delayed work is now not only synchronized and canceled, but also disabled so it will not be re-queued or run again until explicitly re-enabled, which more strongly shuts down TX work processing during close/cancel handling.

grouping_result.intent: Replace TX work cancellation with disable_delayed_work_sync() to fully stop and prevent rescheduling of TLS TX delayed work.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it replaces cancel_delayed_work_sync() with disable_delayed_work_sync() to prevent TLS TX delayed work from being rescheduled and running after TLS context teardown.

candidates.rationale: This is the vulnerable cancellation primitive: it only waits for an in-flight delayed work item to finish, but does not stop the TX work from being re-queued concurrently, which allows tx_work_handler() to run after TLS context teardown has started.

vuln_statements.explanation: This TX work cancellation call is the root cause: it waits for an active delayed work item to finish, but does not disable or prevent concurrent re-queuing of the TLS TX work, so tx_work_handler() can still run after tls_sk_proto_close() has started tearing down the TLS context.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the vulnerable cancellation logic and the fix. The root cause was that `cancel_delayed_work_sync()` on `ctx->tx_work.work` did not stop concurrent re-scheduling. In this commit, `tls_sw_cancel_work_tx()` now does `set_bit(BIT_TX_CLOSING, &ctx->tx_bitmask);` and `set_bit(BIT_TX_SCHEDULED, &ctx->tx_bitmask);` before `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&ctx->tx_work.work);`, and `tx_work_handler()` checks `if (test_bit(BIT_TX_CLOSING, &ctx->tx_bitmask)) return;` before clearing `BIT_TX_SCHEDULED`. That is the fix preventing the work from running after close begins. The old unlock/cancel/relock sequence in `tls_sw_free_resources_tx()` is removed, but the vulnerable construct is still present in the form of `cancel_delayed_work_sync()`; however, it is now guarded by the new closing/scheduled bit handling, so the function already contains the fix.
